title.narrative: Technical and Vocational Education and Training Sector Development Program (TVETSDP)

description.narrative: The proposed Technical and Vocational Education and Training Sector Development Program (TVETSDP) seeks to support the Government of Cambodia in improving access to, and relevance and quality of, the formal technical vocational education and training (TVET) system. The key focus of the project is to achieve a market responsive formal TVET system through partnerships with employers and private sector.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: An accessible, demand-driven TVET system responsive to continuing and emerging labor market demands

By 2023, 60% of regional training center (RTC) and provincial training center (PTC) graduates awarded vocational skills certificate (VSC) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: 2,564 VC graduates (25% female) were enrolled in VC program as of Q2 2022. They are qualified for enrollment in Certificate 1 (CQF Level 2). Data Source: Project quarterly reports

By 2023, Female enrollments in nontraditional skills areas increases from less than 2% to 12% at public TVET institutions Achievement: 22 Progress/Status: There were 1,104 female trainees (or 22%) enrolled in non-traditional skills in AY 2021/2022 vs. 12% of the project target. Cumulative female enrolments in nontraditional skills areas were 6,302 trainees since AY 2013/2014. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

By 2023, 45% increase (35% for females) in enrollments for Cambodia Qualifications Framework (CQF) levels 2-4 training courses at public TVET institutions from an estimated baseline of 918 (197 females) in school year 2011-2012 Achievement: 15856 Progress/Status: There were 6,992 (31% female) trainees enrolled in CQF 2-4 in academic year (AY) 2021/2022. Cumulative enrolments for CQF levels 2-4 training courses are 39,580 trainees (32% female) since AY 2018/19. Data Source: TVET management information system (MIS) data and project quarterly reports
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: 240 female trainees receive accommodation in dormitories at PTCs by 2022 Achievement: 254 Progress/Status: 6 dormitories cumulatively enrolled 388 female trainees attending certificate level courses of priority sectors as of Q4 2021. Women's leadership center management firm (WLCM), which was mobilized in August 2020, support the TTIs hosting the dorms to run career mentorship programs. The WLCM has been extended to other dorms. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: 45% of VSC holders attended center based VSTP in CQF level 2 courses in priority skills areas by 2022 Achievement: 54 Progress/Status: The VSC qualification requirements and guidelines was approved in March 2017, and the Prakas has also been approved in April 2017.
Graduates of first batch of VSC proceeded to CQF Level 2 in AY 2019-2020. The VSC program has been rolled out in May 2019. As of Q2 2022, a total of 2,564 trainees completed VC (CQF level 1) courses of priority sectors and 1,387 trainees (19% females) or 54% of VSC holders enrolled in certificate 1. Data Source: Impact assessment/Project quarterly reports

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: 5,000 people 14-25 (30% female) receive stipends for CQF levels 2-4 training at public TVET institutions by 2021 Achievement: 921 Progress/Status: Guidelines were approved in October 2017. Eligible students enrolled in CQF level 2 through 4 have been assessed for stipends. There were 5,000 students enrolled in CQF 2-4 levels (32% female) had receive stipends as of Q4 2021. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: 50% of CQF level 1 graduates at public TVET institutions assessed for recognition of CQF level 2 competency in the priority skill areas by 2022 Achievement: 54 Progress/Status: Assessment and certification policies were approved by NTB on 20 October 2017. A total of 1,387 out of 2,564 or 54% CQF level 1 graduates were assessed for CQF level 2 enrollment. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: 900 Cambodians assessed for competency in priority sectors by 2022 Achievement: 229 Progress/Status: Guidelines and policies were approved by National Training Board on 20 October 2017.
The certification system was launched in May 2019 at National Polytechnic Institute of Angkor (NPIA), which is an Assessment Center for Construction sector, one of the 5 assessment centers selected by the EA.
As of Q3 2022, there were 900 (16% female) have their skills competencies assessed by the 5 assessment centers. Data Source: Impact assessment/Project quarterly report

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: Women constitute 25% of enrollments at Public TVET Institutions in CQF level 2 training programs in priority skill areas by 2021 Achievement: 25 Progress/Status: There were 726 females or 25% of total trainees enrolled in CQF level 2 in school year 2021/2022. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 10% of urban voucher skills training program (VSTP) courses outsourced to non-state TVET providers by 2021 Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Two out of 21 courses (10%) were outsourced to VSTP non-state TVET providers. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 10,000 trainees (approximately 50% female) supported to participate in skills bridging program (SBP) by 2021 Achievement: 18 Progress/Status: As of Q2 2022, there are 10,000 trainees enrolled in SBP (43% female) or 100% of total target have been enrolled in the SBP under the project. Data Source: Tracer study/project progress reports

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 20% of skills bridging courses outsourced to non-state TVET providers by 2021 Achievement: 40 Progress/Status: 40% of skills bridging courses (115 out of 289) have been outsourced to non-state training providers. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 200 staff from public TVET institutions in Phnom Penh and 50 staff from public TVET institutions in all provinces participate in competency assessment workshops for recognition of competencies by 2021 Achievement: 145 Progress/Status: 200 staff (29% female) from public institutes in Phnom Penh participated in competency-based assessment trainings, and 80 (18% female) staff from provincial TTIs as of Q4 2020. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 50% of TVET instructors at public TVET institutions have their pedagogical and technical knowledges tested using post-training assessment methods and questionnaires developed by the IA's Department of Quality Assurance by 2021 Achievement: 50 Progress/Status: All trained TVET instructors will have their competency tested using post-training assessment tools/method. Competency standards for teachers have been developed and based on HRM Policy framework.
As of Q3 2022, there were 50% or 423 (21% female) of 845 instructors (20.57% female), who had completed two rounds of CBT training in 5 priority sectors, have their technical knowledge assessed. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 55,000 trainees (60% female) supported to participate in VSTP development program in coordination with industry by 2021. Achievement: 549 Progress/Status: As of Q2 2022, there are 55,025 trainees (60% female) enrolled in VSTP training under the project. Data Source: Tracer study/project quarterly report

Output: 2. Improved quality and relevance of TVET system Indicator: 800 RTC and PTC instructors (20% female) trained to deliver competency-based training and assessment for CQF levels 1-4 programs by 2021. Achievement: 63 Progress/Status: As of Q3 2022, 845 (20% female) instructors in priority skill areas have been trained in CBT. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: 1000 public TVET institution trainees (20% female) engaged in internships by 2021 Achievement: 400 Progress/Status: There were 1,000 (21% female) certificate trainees completed a 3-month internship program as of Q2 2022. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 4. Strengthened governance and management of the TVET system Indicator: 30% of RTCs and PTCs engage in revenue-generating activities by 2019 Achievement: 58 Progress/Status: 22 of the 38 EA's training institutes engaged in some sorts of revenue generation. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 4. Strengthened governance and management of the TVET system Indicator: 75% of public TVET institutions use expanded TVET MIS and LMIS to inform TVET programming by 2020 Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All 38 TVET institutes have used improved TVETMIS system under the project. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 4. Strengthened governance and management of the TVET system Indicator: 9,700 Cambodians (30% female) trained at CQF levels 1-4 by PTCs and RTCs by 2021 Achievement: 583 Progress/Status: As of Q3 2022, there were 13,995 Cambodians trained in CQF levels 1-4, of which females are 6,219 (or 44%). Data Source: Program quarterly reports

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: 280 demo-video clips for construction, electrical, auto-mechanics and ICT courses for CQF-2 produced and used as online teaching and learning materials by 2022 Achievement: 195 Progress/Status: 286 demo-video clips have been produced as of Q3 2022 and have been used by TTIs for teaching and learning as well as promote understanding on assessment and certification. Data Source: Project quarterly reports

Output: 1. Increased access to TVET programs Indicator: Module-based learning materials and guidelines for CQF level priority courses developed and used by 2022 Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Production of 20 modular based learning materials for CQF level 2 for automotive electrical servicing, masonry, and computer servicing have been completed in Q1 2022. Training of trainers to deliver the modular-based training has been conducted in March 2022. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: 0 Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: 0 Target year: 2022 Target value: Y Actual value: 20

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: In collaboration with SSCs, VSC (CQF level 1) piloted by 2019 and CQF levels 2-4 training programs in the four priority skill areas developed and piloted by 20 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: 5 modules of manufacturing courses were developed and had been piloted for 162 (19% female) VC trainees, and CBT packages for CQF level 2 courses in manufacturing sector (mechanical equipment and mechatronic servicing courses) have been completed. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: In collaboration with SSCs, four centers of excellence (COEs) representing four priority skill areas developed by 2019 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Construction of all 4 CoEs was completed. They start operation, but require further strengthening and support. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: In collaboration with SSCs, instructor apprenticeship program developed by 2019 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: 256 instructors (14% female) have already completed instructor apprenticeship program. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: In collaboration with SSCs, soft skills training program for CQF levels 1-4 developed and piloted by 2020 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Soft-skills development training module and multi-media materials have been completed as of Q3 2021. Training of Trainers had been completed in Nov. 2021. Soft-skills materials have been uploaded on the project webpage. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: In collaboration with SSCs: CQF level 2 training course in basic manufacturing processes developed and piloted by 2019 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Skills standards, curriculum and assessment packages for electrical and manufacturing certificate 1 training courses were approved by the NTB. Training for instructors on the new packages have been completed after delays due to Covid-19 pandemic. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: In collaboration with SSCs: internship program for CQF levels 3-4 trainees established by 2019 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: 460 (17% female) CQF levels 3-4 trainees completed internship program. Data Source: Project quarterly report Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 3. Increased involvement of employers in TVET delivery Indicator: Internship program in public TVET institutions developed and implemented in collaboration with SSCs by 2019 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Internship policy was approved by the NTB on 20 October 2017.
The internship implementation guidelines and manual aligned with the national internship policy were approved in April 2019.
Data Source: Project quarterly reports Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2014 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
